items.title: Google Ships Gemini 4 Neon as a Coding-Agent Orchestrator
items.summary: On November 18 Google rolled out Gemini 4 Neon across the Gemini API, AI Studio, business tenants, and paid Antigravity and Gemini app tiers. Positioned between Hydrogen (fast execution) and Carbon (hard long-horizon work), Neon brings a one-million-token context, four thinking levels, and pricing of $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 cached, and $15 output. Google reports first place on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (58.6), 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, and 32% lower cost per task than Carbon at the default High setting. In Antigravity, Neon can act as an orchestrator: it plans and reviews while parallel Hydrogen subagents handle routine edits, package updates and test runs, handing control back when they hit trouble. The most revealing number is on SWE-sweep: 12.8% inside the mini-SWE harness versus 39.0% inside Antigravity - same weights, different scaffolding.
items.impact: This is the clearest public demonstration yet that a model score and an agent's actual performance are separate products. Google is selling the orchestration layer and harness, not just weights. Measure cost per verified task on your own repositories before switching tiers - and note that Carbon's promotional $2/$10 rate runs only through November 30, then doubles, which makes this month's token-price comparisons misleading.

items.title: Snap Turns Coding Agents into an AR Publishing Pipeline with Easy Lens CLI
items.summary: Snap launched Easy Lens CLI on November 18: a free, standalone command-line tool that plugs into Claude Code, Cursor and Codex rather than into a vendor GUI. A developer describes a Lens in plain language and the agent runs the entire chain - assembling builds from more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, rendering preview videos, pushing test builds to a phone, fixing errors, publishing through Snap's normal content review, and tracking performance in the same session. Snap says a Web Lens game with leaderboards can go from idea to published in a single day, and cites $1.8 million paid to Lens+ creators last month. Package teardowns flag real limits: the tool is proprietary, ships native binaries only for Apple Silicon macOS, Windows x64 and Linux x64, and its output is confined to the Snapchat mobile app, not SPECS glasses or Camera Kit.
items.impact: The interesting shift is not AR - it is that a platform now treats coding agents as a distribution channel, letting an agent own build, test, release and analytics end to end. Expect more agent-native platform CLIs that bypass vendor tooling. The architecture and lock-in caveats are a useful reminder: agent-accessible does not mean open.

items.title: VS Code 1.147 Lets Agents Use Your Browser as Copilot Adds Adaptive Review and Secret Detection
items.source: GitHub Changelog / VS Code Release Notes / AIDevPulse
items.summary: VS Code 1.147, released as stable on November 18, puts browser use into preview: with the Copilot browser extension, a local harness session and Node.js 22 or later, agents can work directly in your already signed-in Chrome or Edge, while the user finishes sign-in and sensitive steps. Administrators can switch it off with features.browserUse. The release also adds chat.permissions.assisted.instructions, letting teams tell the permission reviewer things like 'always ask before installing packages' - instructions that cannot override permission rules, organization policy or the sandbox. Requests started by other agents are no longer treated as if the user typed them. Separately, GitHub shipped Adaptive code review, which selects Lite, Balanced or Max effort per pull request based on complexity and risk, plus secret detection combining more than 500 known formats with model-based discovery. Claude Code v2.1.327 fixed project-scope mcp add and remove commands wiping unrelated keys in .mcp.json.
items.impact: Earlier agent-security stories here were mostly about agents breaking out; this one is about the controls catching up - explicit permission instructions, effort caps, secret scanning of an agent's own PRs, and harnesses under managed policy. The gap to watch: Claude and Codex harnesses enabled through vscode.allowedHarnesses do not inherit Copilot's managed permission, sandbox, MCP or plugin controls.

items.title: An 84-Page Survey Reframes Embodied AI Around the 'Harness', Not the Model
items.source: Grid Robotics / arXiv / Jiangmen Venture Capital
items.summary: Published on November 19, 'Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems' (arXiv:2611.18359) introduces neither a model nor a benchmark. It defines Agentic Robotics as a three-layer functional stack - S2 for intent, planning, tool calls and verification; S1 for VLA/WAM, navigation, perception and motion planning; S0 for real-time control at 50 Hz to 1 kHz - and argues S2 is a foundation model plus an 'embodied harness': context manager, tool interfaces, planner, memory, verifier and a real-time monitor with hard safety overrides. It proposes capped scaling, meaning capability within a fixed decision deadline, because S2 decisions can take 7.7 to 39.9 seconds while S1 updates at 5 to 200 Hz. In RT-Safe, freezing the simulation while the model thinks produced 19.8% safety success; letting the world keep running dropped it to 0.7% with 12.3 times more collisions. A nine-dimension, 53-sub-item framework separates model ability from closed-loop system performance and calls for a 'Harness Card' with every reported result.
items.impact: This explains directly why coding agents advanced faster than robot agents: code offers auto-verification, vast corpora and resettable sandboxes, and the physical world offers none of them. The takeaway applies to both fields - the harness and verification layer increasingly determines reliability, not the base model. A robotics leaderboard without latency and harness details is close to meaningless.

items.title: Nvidia and AMD Co-Invest as Genesis AI Raises $500M at a $3.5B Valuation
items.summary: Genesis AI, an embodied AI startup founded in March 2025 by Zhou Xian and Theophile Gervet, closed a $500 million Series A at a $3.5 billion post-money valuation, reported on November 18. Investors include Nvidia, AMD, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, Zoom founder Eric Yuan and Yahoo co-founder Jerry Yang - reportedly the first time the two chipmakers have jointly backed an embodied AI company. The team previously built the open-source Genesis physics simulator and released its first embodied foundation model, GENE-26.5, in May. Company-released videos show a single shared-weight model completing more than 20 continuous kitchen subtasks, including one-handed egg cracking and tomato slicing, plus lab work such as pipetting and loading a centrifuge. Its data strategy pairs a data glove with electromagnetic finger tracking and dense tactile sensing against a 1:1, 20-degree-of-freedom dexterous hand, to reduce information loss when transferring human demonstrations to robots.
items.impact: Funding has cooled across embodied AI, so a company under two years old raising at $3.5 billion with both major GPU vendors on the cap table is a strong signal that full-stack 'data plus model plus evaluation plus hardware' bets still command a premium. Treat the demos as vendor claims; the more durable idea is matching the sensing used to collect human data to the actuator that will eventually execute it.
